parsed.reason: The reply has two problems. First, it ends with a question ("Want me to look specifically for parks or playgrounds nearby?") when Hale already has an offerable result — Riverdale Farm — which is described as a "free outdoor farm, open daily." The parent asked for a good park to play nearby, and Riverdale Farm is a real outdoor venue that fits that ask reasonably well. More importantly, Hale also has a second offerable: the Central Library story time, which is indoor and less relevant, but the farm is clearly the right one to lead with. The reply does name the farm correctly. Second, and more critically, the reply says "No parks in what I've got verified" — this frames itself around Hale's internal verification machinery ("what I've got verified"), which is the kind of self-absorbed explanation the rubric penalises. The correct move is simply to offer the farm as the outdoor play option it is, note it's open daily (not just Sun Aug 9 — the offerable says "open daily"), and mention the story time as a bonus if space allows. Pinning it only to "Sun Aug 9" is also slightly off since the offerable says "open daily." The trailing question asking if it should look for parks is odd because it already did and found this — asking to do what it already did is returning the job to the parent. These issues together (self-referential machinery language, incorrect date framing, unnecessary trailing question) bring it to a 3.
